GameSettings

class GameSettings(lang, settings)[source]

Bases: object

KarTEA game configuration: screen, sizes, colors and resources.

A single instance is created by main and injected where needed (GameController, Menu, models, views). There is no global reading: no module imports an already configured GameSettings. Once created, the instance cannot be changed (AttributeError).

The match state (phase/level, score, counters, lane, menu, clock) lives in GameState; data access, in the services.

The class constants below apply to any resolution; the instance attributes depend on the screen and on the player’s configuration. Since the instance is frozen at the end of __init__, all attributes are constants and follow the PEP 8 convention (uppercase).

Parameters:
langstr

Game language.

settingsdict[str, Any]

Effective configuration built by PlayerKarteaConfigService.build_game_settings: screen, calibration points and the player’s configuration already completed with the kartea.ini defaults.

Attributes:
WINDOW_NAME, GAME_TITLEstr, class attribute

Window title (“KarTEA”).

BASE_WIDTH, BASE_HEIGHTint, class attribute

Reference resolution of the original design (800x600).

FPSint, class attribute

Target frames per second (60).

DRAW_FPSbool, class attribute

Whether the FPS counter is drawn.

MAX_DELTA_TIMEfloat, class attribute

Safety cap (s) for GameState.delta_time: avoids big jumps in the game position after a real pause (window switch, loading, debugger breakpoint).

ROAD_WIDTH, SEGMENT_LENGTH, CAMERA_DEPTHint, class attribute

Pseudo-3D road geometry.

DRAW_HITBOXbool, class attribute

Whether the car hitbox is drawn (debugging).

ANIMATION_SPEEDfloat, class attribute

Animation speed.

COLLISION_LANE_TOLERANCEfloat, class attribute

Tolerance (s) of the player lane before an object passes the car. 0 uses only the lane at that instant; > 0 collides if the player was in the object’s lane for most of the last N seconds, absorbing the feet reading jitter near the lane boundary.

OBJECT_SPAWN_SEGMENTSint, class attribute

Segments ahead of the camera where targets, obstacles and the finish line appear.

OBJECT_ARRIVAL_SEGMENTSint, class attribute

Distance (segments) from that point to the front of the car, used to turn the arrival time into speed (measured: ~191 in SVGA, HD and Full HD).

COLORSdict, class attribute

RGB colors of title, score, timer and buttons.

CALIBRATION_POINT_COLOR, CALIBRATION_LINE_COLORtuple, class
attribute

BGR (OpenCV) colors of the calibration area drawn over the camera image: points in red, sides in green.

CONTROL_WIDTH, CONTROL_HEIGHTint, class attribute

Resolution of the control (camera) image used in the mapping.

FEEDBACK_IMAGE_TIME_MIN, FEEDBACK_IMAGE_TIME_MAXfloat, class
attribute

Range (s) of the feedback image display time.

FEET_CLICK_TIME_MIN, FEET_CLICK_TIME_MAXfloat, class attribute

Range (s) of the time standing on a button to select it.

FEET_CLICK_TIME_DEFAULTfloat, class attribute

Default selection time (1.2 s).

FEET_CLICK_BASE_MARGINint, class attribute

Selection hysteresis: once selection starts, the button “grows” this many px (800x600 base) on each side.

FEET_CLICK_EXIT_TOLERANCEfloat, class attribute

Leaving the button for less than this time (s) does not interrupt the count.

FEET_MARKER_BASE_RADIUSint, class attribute

Radius of the feet dot (800x600 base).

FEET_MARKER_COLOR, FEET_MARKER_BORDER_COLORtuple, class attribute

RGB colors of the feet dot and its border.

BASE_OBJ_POSlist[tuple[int, int]], class attribute

Reference positions (800x600) where objects appear, per lane.

CURRENT_LANGstr

Game language.

SCREEN_WIDTH, SCREEN_HEIGHTint

Screen size (px).

SCREEN_OS_INDEX, SCREEN_POS_X, SCREEN_POS_Yint

Monitor index and window position.

FULLSCREENbool

Whether the game runs fullscreen.

CALIBRATION_POINTSnumpy.ndarray

Read-only 4x2 int array with the calibrated area; zeros when there is no calibration.

LANE_DIV_0, LANE_DIV_1, LANE_DIV_2, LANE_DIV_3int

Screen x of the lane boundaries (thirds of the width).

UI_SCALEfloat

UI scale factor (smallest of the width/height scales, so nothing is distorted).

WIDTH_RATIO, HEIGHT_RATIOfloat

Camera -> screen mapping; without it the car cannot cross the whole screen at resolutions other than 800x600.

BUTTONS_SIZEStuple[int, int]

Menu button size, scaled.

FONTSdict[str, pygame.font.Font]

“small”, “medium” and “big” fonts, scaled.

CAR_SIZEint

Car size (1/5 of the screen width).

CAR_HITBOX_SIZEtuple[int, int]

Car hitbox size.

TARGETS_SIZES, OBSTACLE_SIZEStuple[int, int]

Size of targets and obstacles before perspective (100x100).

OBJ_POSlist[tuple[int, int]]

BASE_OBJ_POS scaled to the screen.

VEHICLE_IMAGE, ENVIRONMENT_IMAGE_RIGHT, ENVIRONMENT_IMAGE_LEFTstr

Resolved paths (“:/…” or mods file) of the image resources.

HORIZON_IMAGEstr

Resolved path of the horizon (environment background) image.

TARGET_IMAGE, OBSTACLE_IMAGEstr

Resolved paths of the target and obstacle images.

POSITIVE_FEEDBACK_IMAGE, NEUTRAL_FEEDBACK_IMAGEstr

Resolved paths of the feedback images (also NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK_IMAGE).

POSITIVE_FEEDBACK_SOUND, NEUTRAL_FEEDBACK_SOUNDstr

Resolved paths of the feedback sounds (also NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK_SOUND).

FEEDBACK_IMAGE_TIMEfloat

Time (s) the positive/negative feedback image stays on screen, clamped to the allowed range.

FEET_CLICK_TIMEfloat

Time (s) on a button to select it with the feet, clamped.

FEET_CLICK_MARGINint

FEET_CLICK_BASE_MARGIN scaled.

FEET_MARKER_RADIUSint

Radius of the feet dot, scaled (at least 4 px).

OBJECT_ARRIVAL_TIMEMapping[int, float]

Read-only {speed: seconds} from the player’s configuration.

PALETTEint

Number of the track color palette (KarteaPalettes).

MENU_BACKGROUND, MENU_FEEDBACK_25, MENU_FEEDBACK_50str

Built-in menu images (also MENU_FEEDBACK_75).

MENU_CLICK_SOUNDstr

Menu’s own click sound (“click” alias in the QRC), independent of the player’s positive feedback sound.

MISS_SOUND, POINT_SOUNDstr

Miss and hit sounds: the player’s negative and positive feedback sounds.

CRASH_SOUND, WIN_SOUND, CLOCK_TICK_SOUNDstr

Sounds of the user’s sounds folder.

FINISH_IMAGEstr

Built-in finish line image.

HORIZON_BG_IMAGEstr

Horizon image: HORIZON_IMAGE or, if it does not resolve, the built-in “horizon”.

Notes

Speed is defined by the ARRIVAL (reaction) TIME: seconds between an object appearing on the road and reaching the front of the car. Since the road advances by delta-time (real seconds), the time is the same on any machine, FPS and resolution; FPS only affects the visual smoothness. The speed range of each level (1, 2 or 3) comes from LevelRules.speed; the time of each range comes from the player’s configuration, clamped and ordered by KarteaArrivalTimeFields.order.

Collision is decided by LANE: when the base of a target/obstacle passes the front of the car, it collides if the player is in the object’s lane (see COLLISION_LANE_TOLERANCE); it does not depend on resolution, image sizes, depth or FPS.

Each resource field of KarteaResourceFields.ALL becomes an uppercase attribute. The configuration stores the name chosen on the screen (built-in alias, e.g. “defaultvehicle”, or mods file, e.g. “mycar.png”); here it becomes the path to load. If the name no longer exists (e.g. a file deleted from mods), the field default is used.
